name: Muhammad
role: Prophet of Islam; founder and ruler of the Medinan state (c. 571-632)
summary: Muhammad proclaimed the Quran as divine revelation and led the community in Medina as religious teacher, lawgiver, judge and military commander. His recorded positions combine religious law, mutual defence and welfare duties such as zakat with a ban on interest. He ruled through a covenant that included Jewish tribes as allies, and later expelled or fought some of them.

property-fundamental.rationale: Farewell Sermon (Sahih Muslim 15:159): "your blood, your property are as sacred and inviolable"; Quran 4:29 forbids consuming wealth unjustly. Zakat and fifths of spoils (59:7) qualify this.

cut-welfare.rationale: He instituted zakat, an obligatory levy distributed first to the poor and needy (Quran 9:60, 59:7); Bukhari 1470 separately praises earning over begging.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Quran 5:90 calls intoxicants "defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it". Drugs other than wine are not named.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Quran 24:2 and 17:32 prohibit sex outside marriage; Bukhari 2237 reports he forbade the earnings of prostitution; Quran 24:33 forbids compelling slave women into prostitution.

traditional-family.rationale: Quran 4:1 and 30:21 set marriage and kinship as the basis of the community; 17:23 on parents. He regulated marriage, dower and inheritance.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred: Quran 7:80-81 condemns men approaching men instead of women, and marriage in 30:21 is between mates from different sexes. He did not address same-sex marriage as such.

more-religion-public.rationale: He made religion the organising basis of the Medinan community (Constitution clause 2, the ummah) and governed by revealed law.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Quran 4:75 asks why believers do not fight for the oppressed men, women and children who cry out for deliverance.

revolution-justified.rationale: He overturned the Quraysh order at Mecca by force after emigrating, and Quran 22:39-40 permits fighting those who expelled the believers. This is a religious-political conquest, not an uprising against a government as such.

political-violence-never.rationale: He proclaimed permission to fight those who wronged the believers (Quran 22:39, 2:190) and led or sent armed expeditions as ruler of Medina, so he did not hold that political violence is never justified.

separate-church-state.rationale: He combined religious and political authority in Medina; the Constitution refers disputes to God and Muhammad and Quran 5:48 tells him to rule by revelation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Quran 5:48 instructs him to judge between people by what Allah has revealed (also 5:44-47); the Constitution of Medina refers disputes to God and Muhammad. He governed Medina by the revealed text.

military-superiority.rationale: Quran 8:60 tells believers to prepare whatever force they can, to deter enemies.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Quran 43:32 states God raised some above others in livelihood and rank; 4:32 tells people not to covet what others have been given.

civilizational-union.rationale: Quran 49:10 says believers are brothers and 21:92 calls the community one ummah; the Constitution makes believers one political unit distinct from others.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Quran 17:44 and 24:41 say all things in the heavens and earth glorify God, giving creation worth beyond human use; 55:10 says the earth was set down for creatures.

taxation-theft.rationale: Quran 9:103 tells him to take zakat from believers' wealth and 9:60 lists collectors among its recipients; he levied zakat as an obligation. Zakat is framed as a religious duty, so medium.

conscription.rationale: He mobilised the community for Tabuk and the Quran rebukes and threatens those who held back (9:38-39, 9:81-83); the Constitution says none may go out to fight without his permission.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Medinan state grew across Arabia under him (Khaybar, Mecca, Tabuk, tribal submissions), but this was also defended as defence of the community, so contested.

universal-morality.rationale: Quran 91:7-8 says the soul was inspired with its wickedness and righteousness and 30:30 points to a natural disposition; 7:157 speaks of commanding what is known as right.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Quran 2:3 praises belief in the unseen and revelation is the guide (4:59); the Quran also urges reflection, but faith in revelation is primary.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Quran 4:34 says men are in charge of women with maintenance duties; 4:11 and 2:282 give different shares and testimony weights. The Farewell Sermon gives husbands and wives distinct rights and duties.

ban-interest.rationale: Quran 2:275: "Allah has permitted trade and forbidden interest"; 2:278-279 demand giving up outstanding interest. In the Farewell Sermon (Sahih Muslim 15:159) he abolished pre-Islamic usury, starting with that owed to his uncle al-Abbas.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inferred: Quran 49:13 makes peoples and tribes distinct only so they may know one another, with nobility by righteousness; no racial legal separation is recorded.

national-mission.rationale: No recorded position on spreading a form of government; the call to spread the religion (Quran 3:110, 9:33) is about something nearby.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Quran 49:13 says the most noble before God is the most righteous, and the Farewell Sermon reports equal rights of spouses; law nonetheless differed by sex, status and faith, so low.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Constitution of Medina lets the Jewish tribes keep their own religion and bear their own expenses; Quran 5:42-43 lets him judge between them or decline. Law was partly separate by community.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Quran 6:142-144 lists cattle, sheep, goats and camels as lawful for food and 5:1 declares livestock lawful; he sanctioned slaughter of cattle rather than banning it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Contested: Quran 42:38 and 3:159 call for consultation, and allegiance pledges were taken from followers, but his authority rested on his claim of divine commission (4:59).

population-transfer.rationale: Wikipedia records that he expelled the Banu Qaynuqa and the Banu Nadir from Medina after they were judged to have broken the covenant (some historians date the first after his death); Bukhari/Muslim report him saying he would expel Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula (Muslim 4594 in this edition).

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Wikipedia's account records that he launched raids on Meccan caravans from Medina and later marched on Mecca; Quran 2:190 forbids transgression, so the record points both ways but includes initiating force.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Quran 9:60 lists the poor and needy first among zakat recipients and 59:7 says wealth should not circulate only among the rich.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The record shows him commanding the Medinan forces and appointing commanders and officials; there was no legislature.

death-penalty.rationale: Quran 5:33 prescribes killing or crucifixion for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and spread corruption; 2:178 and Constitution of Medina clause on intentional murder prescribe retaliation by death unless the heir accepts blood money.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Quran 59:7 gives state-held fai to orphans, the needy and travellers "so that it will not be a perpetual distribution among the rich"; zakat takes a share of private wealth for set recipients (9:60, 9:103).

collective-defense.rationale: Constitution of Medina: the signatories "shall have each other's help in the event of any force invading Yathrib" and if anyone fights the people of the code their mutual help applies.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine descent is rejected: Quran 18:110 "I am only a man like you" and 112:3 "He neither begets nor is born"; Bukhari 3445 has him calling himself a slave of God.

leader-cult.rationale: Bukhari 3445 reports him saying "Do not exaggerate in praising me as the Christians praised the son of Mary, for I am only a Slave"; Quran 18:110: "I am only a man like you".

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contested: Bukhari 6922 reports him saying "Whoever changed his Islamic religion, then kill him", while Quran 2:256 says there is no compulsion in religion and prescribes no worldly penalty for apostasy.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Bukhari 7056 reports the allegiance he took required listening and obeying rulers unless one saw clear disbelief with proof from God; resisting a ruler merely for lawbreaking is not endorsed.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Bukhari 3318 reports a woman entering Hell over a cat she tied and starved.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Quran 6:142-144 permits livestock for food; Muslim 5055 (in this edition) reports him saying to slaughter in a good way, sharpen the knife and let the animal die comfortably.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Quran 51:19 and 70:24-25 say the beggar and the deprived have a right in the wealth of the well-off; 17:26 commands giving relatives, the needy and the traveller their due.

filial-duty.rationale: Quran 17:23: parents are to be treated well, never rebuked, even in old age; also 31:14 and 46:15.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Contested: Quran 2:236 and 2:229 let a husband divorce without a stated fault, but a wife's exit is conditional (2:229 on her giving up property).

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Quran 102:1 says competition in worldly increase diverts people, and 57:20 calls worldly life rivalry in wealth and children; 9:34 warns hoarders.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Quran 4:59 commands obedience to Allah, the Messenger and those in authority; Bukhari 7144 limits this only where orders involve disobedience to God.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Contested: the Constitution treats the Jewish tribes as allies, while Quran 5:82 and the accounts of Banu Nadir and Banu Qurayza describe some Jewish tribes as covenant-breakers.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Quran 4:4 and 4:20-21 require a dower and treat marriage as a contract with legal rights, and 4:12 gives spouses inheritance.

religious-nation.rationale: Contested: the Constitution makes the Muslim believers one ummah distinct from others, yet counts Jewish tribes as "one community with the believers", each keeping its own religion.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred: he presented religion as true divine revelation (Quran 18:110), not as an illusion that fades with material improvement.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Quran 7:80-81 condemns men approaching men; 4:16 prescribes punishment for "the two who commit it" without naming the penalty and its reference is debated. No clear legal penalty in the Quran.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Contested: Quran 9:73 orders striving against hypocrites and 9:107 describes a rival mosque, yet the Medina record shows he left known hypocrites such as Abdullah ibn Ubayy unpunished, and the Mecca amnesty spared most opponents.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Contested: Quran 6:108 tells believers not to revile what others invoke, but 9:12 threatens treaty-breakers who defame the religion, and the Mecca account records some who insulted him being excluded from the amnesty.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Quran 2:190 and 22:39 permit fighting those who fight or wrong the believers, and 9:38-39 rebukes those who do not go forth when called; an obligation on every Muslim is stated only for mobilisations he called.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Contested: Quran 5:44 calls those who do not judge by revelation disbelievers, but Bukhari 7056 permits resistance only for clear disbelief, and Muslim reports obeying rulers who still pray.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Quran 12:40: "Legislation is not but for Allah"; 4:59 ties obedience to those in authority to obedience to Allah and the Messenger.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He maintained an army in Medina and Quran 8:60 tells believers to prepare all the force they can.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Quran 2:221 forbids marrying polytheists, while 5:5 permits marrying chaste women of the People of the Book; marriage across religions is partly restricted.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: he proclaimed belief in one God as true and condemned disbelief (Quran 18:110, 2:256 on faith by choice), so state promotion of atheism follows as opposed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Contested: Quran praises private giving (2:261), yet 9:103 and 9:60 set a collected, officially administered zakat for the poor.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Quran 4:34 says men are in charge of women, and 2:228 says men have a degree over them, alongside similar rights; the Farewell Sermon assigns the husband authority over household access.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Quran 22:39 permits fighting by those attacked; Bukhari 2480 reports him saying whoever is killed protecting his property is a martyr. He endorsed defensive killing.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Quran 15:29 speaks of God breathing spirit into humans, and 2:201 asks for good in this world and the next; the Constitution joins worship and communal governance.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Contested: Quran 2:190 limits fighting to those who fight you and 22:39 permits it to the wronged, while 9:29 and the campaigns against Khaybar, Mecca and Tabuk went beyond immediate defence.

arms-reduction.rationale: Quran 8:60 tells believers to prepare all the power and steeds of war they are able, not to reduce arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Quran 9:38-39 criticises those who hold back when called to fight; he expected obedience in his campaigns.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Quran 30:30 refers to the fitrah on which God created people and says no change should be in the creation of Allah; 4:119 treats altering it as Satan's command.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Contested: Quran 42:13 and 21:25 say all messengers brought the same message of one God, but 3:85 rejects any way other than Islam.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Quran 4:7 and 4:11-12 give women an inheritance share, but generally half of a male relative's. A right to inherit exists; equality of that right does not, so contested.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: No recorded position on sentencing repeat offenders; the fixed penalties in Quran 5:38 and 24:2 are about something nearby.

premarital-sex.rationale: Quran 24:2 prescribes a hundred lashes for unmarried women and men guilty of sexual intercourse, and 17:32 says not to approach unlawful sexual intercourse.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Bukhari 2335: "He who cultivates land that does not belong to anybody is more rightful to own it."

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Quran 4:82 says it has no discrepancy and he proclaimed it as the word of God; its literal reading is qualified by 3:7 on clear and allegorical verses.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Bukhari 7144 reports him saying a Muslim must obey the ruler unless ordered to disobey Allah, in which case one should not obey. Close but not the same as a law being void.

notes: Quran treated as his proclaimed words; hadith (Bukhari, Muslim) are later reports and capped at medium or low. sunnah.com was unreachable (Cloudflare challenge), so hadith text came from a GitHub-hosted mirror. Several verses and reports point in different directions on apostasy, blasphemy and war; those are answered 0 or low. Later jurists' rulings are not used.
